messages:
maria (oncall): Alert: spike in KV cache size + continuous-batching errors. Getting 5xxs from streaming path, token cadence stalling for some requests. Paging going crazy on kvcache-01. Incident bot posted metrics.
incidents-bot: [ALERT] kvcache.evictions.rate > 2000/s on kvcache-01. streaming.latency.p95 doubled in last 3m. Severity: P1.
maria (oncall): Noted. Triage in thread. @ops-sre can you check paging/eviction counters and any recent deploys?
ops-sre: Looking. No code deploys in last 30m. I see sudden rise in prefetch hits and continuous_batch queue length. kvcache memory usage at 92% on node set, eviction loop running hot.
ajay: Paging/thrash looks correlated with a recent config change to prefetch window at 1.5x. We pushed that as an experiment earlier today for perf. Rolling that back would be low risk. Also see streaming worker threads showing partial flush warnings in logs.
leo: I can roll back the prefetch delta. Rolling to previous prefetch-window=1.0 on canary group now. Command: `rbctl set prefetch_window=1.0 --subset=canary-kv`
maria (oncall): Good. Do it for canary first, then global if it helps. Also, we should throttle continuous-batching to reduce batch amplification. Set `continuous_batch.max_tokens=512` and `cadence.ms=10` maybe.
sam (eng): I can patch cadence. Applying `continuous_batch.cadence_ms=10` on canary streaming nodes. Patch applied to two canary pods. Observing logs.
ops-sre: After canary rollback to prefetch=1.0, eviction rate on canary nodes dropped ~60% within 40s. Streaming p95 on canary back to baseline. 
maria (oncall): Ok this suggests prefetch change is primary trigger. @tess (support) start drafting customer impact note: brief summary, affected endpoints, mitigation plan.
tess (support): Drafting now. Which customers saw errors? Any externally visible 5xxs or just increased latency?
customer-success: We are seeing support tickets from two customers reporting token stream stalls and aborted responses around 16:22 UTC. They are on Dedicated capacity in us-west. Please include them in impact note.
ajay: Additional data: continuous batch queue depth was spiking due to longer KV lookup latency; combined with larger prefetch window we amplified backend hits causing paging thrash and partial flush bug surfaced — some streaming sessions ended up with stale KV pages leading to token cadence stalls.
leo: I found the partial flush stacktrace in streaming logs: `PartialFlushException: flush_incomplete at kv_cache_paging.cc:412` repeated during the spike. Looks like eviction + partial flush race.
maria (oncall): Mitigations complete on canary. We should promote rollback globally and also increase eviction soft limit to avoid immediate thrash while we investigate. Plan: 1) global rollback prefetch->1.0 2) set eviction.soft_limit=0.88 3) reduce continuous_batch.max_tokens to 512 4) follow-up postmortem.
ops-sre: Rolling global prefetch rollback now (`rbctl set prefetch_window=1.0 --subset=all`) — doing in waves. Patch eviction.soft_limit=0.88 concurrently to give breathing room.
sam (eng): Applying batch throttle across streaming fleet. `kubectl apply -f continuous-batch-throttle.yml` on prod. Confirmed applied.
ops-sre: Eviction rate back down cluster-wide in ~2m. Streaming p95 improving. Some residual 5xxs but decreasing.
maria (oncall): Good. @customer-success please send interim note: "We're investigating increased latency and intermittent aborted streaming responses from ~16:20-16:35 UTC for some us-west dedicated customers. Mitigation in progress; rolling back experimental prefetch and throttling batch cadence. We'll follow up with full root cause.":thumbsup:
tess (support): Sent to affected customers. Included request id examples and recommended temporary retry behavior.
customer-success: Customers acknowledged. One customer asked if this will recur — told them we are rolling back the change and adding safety caps.
ajay: Root cause hypothesis: aggressive prefetch + continuous batching interacts suboptimally under KV page misses, causing cascading increased KV latency, eviction storms, and a partial flush race that stalls token cadence. The prefetch multiplier increased number of concurrent page fetches beyond the KV cache's paging IOPS envelope.
leo: Action items off this thread: 1) revert prefetch experiment permanently until vetted 2) add a prefetch throttler to bound concurrent prefetches 3) add realtime alerting for partial flush exceptions 4) add a canary that simulates high miss-rate to catch regressions 5) postmortem and retro.
maria (oncall): I'll open the incident ticket and assign owners. Incident ticket: INC-2026-0425. Owners: ajay (root cause), leo (fix partial flush), ops-sre (safety caps + rollback validation), tess/customer-success (customer comms).
incidents-bot: Incident INC-2026-0425 created. Priority P1 -> Status: mitigated (actions applied). Link: https://incidents.internal/INC-2026-0425
maria (oncall): Handoff to next oncall in 30m. @ops-sre please include logs and timeline in ticket. Also capture exact rollbacks + config diffs.
ops-sre: Will attach diffs and timeline. Key diffs: prefetch_window: 1.5 -> 1.0 (global), continuous_batch.cadence_ms: 2 -> 10 (canary->global), continuous_batch.max_tokens: 2048 -> 512, eviction.soft_limit: 0.80 -> 0.88.
sam (eng): I'll begin work on prefetch throttler PR and instrumenting concurrent prefetch counter metrics. Will post link shortly.
leo: Also adding unit test to simulate partial flush under eviction backpressure.
maria (oncall): Thanks team. Leaving notes in incident ticket then marking this thread for follow-up. If anything re-spikes ping with `@maria` and escalate.
ops-sre: Final update: mitigation rolled, error rate back to baseline, customers notified. Closing on-call handoff.
